::: {#rem-memorization}

#### Overfitting and memorization

@yeom2018privacy [section 3.2] show that if an attack guesses "trained on" whenever a classifier is right,
the share of training points it flags minus the share of other points it flags
equals the classifier's [generalization gap](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-generalization-gap) in [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy).
The network of @sol-membership is right on `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$member_acc)` of its training digits
and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$outsider_acc)` of the others,
so that guess is right `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 50 * (1 + py$member_acc - py$outsider_acc))` of the time on a half-and-half set.
A network that [overfits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-overfitting) gives away more about its [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set).

[Large language model](applications.qmd#def-large-language-model)s can give away the training text itself.
@carlini2021extracting generated text from GPT-2
and found 604 passages copied word for word from its [training data](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set),
including names, phone numbers and email addresses,
even text that appeared in only one document of the training data.
[Ethics and Fairness](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/ethics.html#misinformation-and-privacy) in the DATA 571 notes covers the privacy risk,
and differential privacy,
a way to train that limits it.

:::
